visuals.title: Where PV shows itself
visuals.text: Headache and dizziness, visual loss, tinnitus, facial plethora, itch after a hot bath, burning hands and feet, a LUQ spleen.

visuals.title: Thick blood clots everywhere
visuals.text: Stroke, MI, DVT/PE and Budd-Chiari (hepatic vein clot); also gout.

glossary.Red cell mass: The total volume of red blood cells in the body.
glossary.Thrombosis: Formation of a blood clot inside a vessel.
glossary.Primary: Arising from the tissue itself, here the bone marrow, rather than as a response to something else.
glossary.Tinnitus: Ringing or buzzing in the ears.
glossary.Facial plethora: A red, flushed face from too many red blood cells.
glossary.LUQ: Left upper quadrant of the abdomen, where an enlarged spleen is felt.
glossary.Platelets: Small cell fragments that help blood clot.
glossary.Hb: Haemoglobin, the oxygen-carrying protein in red cells.
glossary.Serum: The liquid part of blood left after it clots, used for many blood tests.
glossary.Obesity: Excess body fat, usually a BMI of 30 or more.
glossary.Chronic hypoxia: Long-term low oxygen levels in the body's tissues.
glossary.High altitude: Living or staying high above sea level, where there is less oxygen.
glossary.O2 sats: Oxygen saturation: the percentage of haemoglobin carrying oxygen, measured with a finger probe.
glossary.DVT: Deep vein thrombosis: a clot in a deep vein, usually in the leg.
glossary.PE: Pulmonary embolism: a clot blocking an artery in the lungs.
glossary.Stroke: Brain damage from a blocked or burst blood vessel.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: measures red cells, white cells, platelets and haemoglobin.
glossary.Antiplatelet: A drug that stops platelets sticking together, reducing clots.
glossary.Oxygenation: Getting enough oxygen into the blood.
glossary.Erythroid progenitors: Early marrow cells that develop into red blood cells.
glossary.Clonal: Coming from a single abnormal cell and its copies.
glossary.Tissue hypoxia: Too little oxygen reaching the body's tissues.
glossary.Ectopic: Produced in an abnormal place, e.g. EPO made by a tumour rather than the kidney.
glossary.Compensatory: A response by the body to make up for a problem.
glossary.Microcirculatory flow: Blood flow through the smallest vessels, the capillaries.
glossary.Mast cells: Immune cells in tissues that release histamine, causing itch and swelling.
glossary.Basophils: White blood cells that release histamine.
glossary.Arterial thrombosis: A clot in an artery, causing stroke or heart attack.
glossary.Venous thrombosis: A clot in a vein, such as a DVT.
